chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadala, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Any man who buys something that has a defect or a flaw, which was not made clear to him, and he alters it after taking possession, then learns of that flaw or defect, the sale is confirmed upon him, and he is refunded an amount corresponding to the deficiency caused by that defect and flaw in the price, had it not had that defect.

key_terms.بِقَدْرِ مَا يَنْقُصُ: According to the amount of deficiency
key_terms.عَوَارٌ: Flaw or defect (often implying something more significant or rectifiable)
key_terms.يُمْضَى عَلَيْهِ الْبَيْعُ: The sale is confirmed/validated upon him

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when a buyer finds a hidden defect in an item after altering it?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the principle of 'khiyar al-ayb' (option of defect), establishing that if a buyer alters an item before discovering a hidden flaw, the sale is not voided but rather adjusted via a proportional deduction from the price. This ruling, preserved in al-Kafi, reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on fairness in commercial transactions, ensuring the seller compensates for the diminished value without penalizing the buyer for their prior use or modification of the goods.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Fazalat, from Musa Bin Bakr, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Whichever man buys something and there is a defect in it, or a flaw which cannot be rectified, and it was not made apparent to him, so he does something in it after having taken possession of the thing, then he came to know that flaw, or that disorder, the sale would be concluded upon him in accordance with what was deficient from that disorder and the defact, from the price of that, if there did not happen to be with it (a discount for the defact)’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadalah from Musa ibn Bakr from Zurarah who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

Whoever buys something and finds defect in it or injuries that does not get well which was not apparent to him (when buying) and he then does some changes in it after taking delivery then finds out about the defect or injury, he must approve the sale and ask for the refund of the cost of the defect or injury from the price of the item (he has paid).”’
